articles.title: La corrección del error en XRP Ledger se pospone hasta noviembre tras una caída de soporte de los validadores durante dos horas
articles.text:
La corrección del error en XRP Ledger se pospuso para noviembre tras una caída en el apoyo de los validadores durante dos horas
La solución perdió su cuenta regresiva de dos semanas a menos de dos días del final, después de que el apoyo cayera a 26 de 35 validadores. Ahora ha vuelto a 31.
- Una breve caída en el soporte de los validadores reinició el período de aprobación requerido de 14 días para la corrección del error en XRP Ledger, retrasando la activación del 23 de octubre al 4 de noviembre.
- El apoyo a la solución ha aumentado a 31 de 35 validadores confiables, dos más que los 29 necesarios para mantener el umbral de aprobación de la red.
- El parche cierra una brecha en la creación de tokens y ajusta los cálculos de la bóveda y los préstamos, aunque el sistema de préstamos en general no ha obtenido suficiente apoyo de los validadores para iniciar su propia cuenta regresiva de activación.
Una oscilación de dos horas en el apoyo de los validadores ha retrasado la última corrección de errores del XRP Ledger hasta noviembre, menos de dos días antes de la fecha prevista para su activación.
Los validadores son los servidores independientes que acuerdan qué transacciones cuentan. Cambiar las reglas de la red requiere el respaldo de más del 80% de los 35 en los que la red confía por defecto, lo que equivale a 29.
Ese soporte se verifica aproximadamente cada 15 minutos, y debe mantenerse en cada una de las verificaciones durante 14 días consecutivos. Si falla una vez, aunque sea brevemente, el contador vuelve a cero.
La solución, denominada fixCleanup3_4_0, no tenía espacio para eso. Se mantuvo exactamente en 29 votos el lunes, con la activación prevista para las 09:34 UTC del 23 de octubre. En un punto de control a las 12:54 UTC del miércoles, solo 26 validadores estaban votando a favor, según Panel de Control XRPL.
Para las 14:46 UTC, el conteo volvió a 29 y comenzó una nueva cuenta regresiva. XRPLWin ahora enumera la corrección como activa a las 14:46 UTC del 4 de noviembre. El respaldo ha aumentado desde entonces a 31 de 35, por lo que la corrección entra en su segunda ejecución con dos votos de margen (la primera vez no tuvo ninguno).
Sin embargo, ninguno de los rastreadores muestra qué validadores se desconectaron. Los votos solo cuentan de los validadores de los que la red recibe efectivamente noticias en cada verificación, por lo que un servidor que estuvo fuera de línea o reiniciándose en el momento incorrecto cuenta igual que un no.
El parche cierra un vacío legal que podría permitir que una cuenta autorizada únicamente para quemar, o destruir, los tokens de un emisor cree nuevos bajo ciertas condiciones, según el notas de la versión 3.4.0 de xrpld, y cómo el código de préstamos determina cuándo un préstamo está atrasado o en incumplimiento.
Este código pertenece a la sistema Ripple ha propuesto a bancos y compañías de pago desde junio, donde los prestamistas almacenan XRP u otros tokens en bóvedas y un corredor los presta por un plazo fijo. Aún no está operativo al cierre del jueves.

articles.title: Bitcoin cede sus ganancias tras alcanzar los $85,000, mientras Tesla y Meta no logran calmar las inquietudes sobre la IA
articles.text:
Bitcoin cede su avance hacia los $85,000 mientras Tesla y Meta no logran calmar los nervios por la IA
BTC rompió su techo de $84,000 a última hora del miércoles, para luego retroceder al soporte de $82,500 que los analistas están observando, en medio de la caída de los futuros tecnológicos.
- Bitcoin cotizó justo por debajo de $82,800 después de que un breve repunte a casi $85,000 se revirtiera, dejando a la criptomoneda cerca de un nivel clave de soporte en $82,500 que algunos analistas señalan podría preceder a una caída hacia $70,000.
- La mayoría de las principales criptomonedas disminuyeron, con HYPE, Dogecoin y Solana entre las más rezagadas, mientras que Zcash ganó casi un 3% y XRP registró un leve aumento.
- Perspectivas corporativas decepcionantes y dudas renovadas sobre el gasto en inteligencia artificial afectaron a los futuros de acciones en Estados Unidos y a los mercados asiáticos, mientras el petróleo subía en medio de nuevas tensiones en Medio Oriente.
Bitcoin se mantuvo estable justo por debajo de los 82,800 USD en las horas de la mañana del jueves en Asia, después de ceder el repunte de última hora del miércoles que lo llevó a cerca de 85,000 USD. Resultados diversos de Tesla y Meta empujaron a la baja los futuros del Nasdaq y reavivaron las dudas sobre el comercio relacionado con la IA.
ZEC fue el único ganador destacado entre las principales, subiendo casi un 3% hasta cerca de $1,290, y XRP añadió menos del 1%. HYPE fue el rezagado, cayendo un 3% hasta aproximadamente $79. DOGE bajó un 2% y SOL perdió cerca de un 1%, mientras que ether, BNB y TRX descendieron menos del 1%, según datos de CoinDesk.
El repunte no duró mucho. Bitcoin superó los $84,000, el techo que lo detuvo el 13 y 14 de octubre, y alcanzó un máximo cercano a $84,800 la noche del miércoles. En unas seis horas, cayó más de $2,000 hasta aproximadamente $82,600, una noche difícil para quienes persiguieron el movimiento.
Eso deja a bitcoin en $82,500, un nivel que algunos observadores del mercado advierten podría desencadenar una caída hacia $70,000 si se rompe de manera definitiva.
Las grandes tecnológicas no ayudaron. Tesla cayó un 3% en las operaciones fuera de horario después de recortar su previsión de gasto de capital, y el fabricante de equipos para chips Lam Research bajó un 7% debido a unas perspectivas débiles.
Meta subió un 2% tras aumentar sus planes de gasto en IA, pero eso no fue suficiente para mejorar el ánimo. Los futuros del Nasdaq 100 cayeron un 1,1% y los futuros del S&P 500 perdieron un 0,5%.
Asia lo sufrió considerablemente. El Kospi de Corea del Sur cayó un 2.2% debido a la retirada de Samsung Electronics y SK Hynix, mientras que el CSI 300 de China descendió un 1.7%, encaminándose hacia un mercado bajista. Alibaba lideró la caída de las acciones del comercio electrónico chino después de que el gobierno solicitara un control de calidad más estricto. El crudo subió tras un nuevo aumento de tensiones en Oriente Medio.

articles.title: Hegseth Bans Pentagon Insider Bets on Military Operations
articles.text:
Pentagon bans US forces from using military info to bet in prediction markets
Hegseth warned that prediction market wagers could expose military operations to adversaries.
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has barred all Pentagon staff from using undisclosed information to place wagers on upcoming military action, including on prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket.
In a memo sent to senior Pentagon and defense agencies on Tuesday, Hegseth said all Department of War personnel are prohibited from engaging in financial transactions using nonpublic information. This involves both classified and unclassified information.
“Make no mistake why this matters. Our enemies watch movements in these markets,” Hegseth wrote. “The lives of our Service members often depend on the enemy not knowing what is coming.”
“Beyond operational security, financial stakes can warp judgment. A logistician with money riding on a strike date has an interest in that date. An analyst with a position on an outcome has an interest in that outcome,” he said.
The directive follows the April indictment of US Army soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who allegedly used classified information about the operation to capture Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro to make more than $400,000 on Polymarket.
Prosecutors allege Van Dyke participated in planning and executing the operation, then used his advance knowledge to wager on outcomes related to Maduro’s removal. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges.
In February, Israeli authorities arrested and indicted a military reservist and a civilian for allegedly using classified information to place bets on Polymarket related to Israeli military strikes on Iran.
Related: CFTC, US soldier accused of illegal Polymarket bet spar over interpretation of prediction markets

articles.title: New DeepSeek Ban In US, Swiss-Asia Crypto Ties Deepen: Asia Express
articles.text:
New DeepSeek ban in US, Swiss-Asia crypto ties deepen: Asia Express
DeepSeek banned from US federal civilian agencies over spying fears. Singapore firm behind Europe’s only spot Bitcoin ETF, as Switzerland partners with Vietnam on crypto tech.
CHINA
Treasury proposes blocks on US investments in AI and semiconductors in some foreign countries
The US Treasury has proposed new rules that would block investment in artificial intelligence projects (sorry, ‘Super Intelligence’ projects) and certain high risk semiconductors in some foreign countries.
The blocks have been mainly aimed at geopolitical rival China, but will now also encompass other adversaries including Russia, Iran, North Korea and Cuba. The rules would implement the COINS Act from December 2025 and expand the Outbound Investment Security Program that went into effect in January 2025.
They rules build on previous restrictions on selling high powered AI chips to China. The US is backing up its threats too, having announced the first $200,000 penalty this month to Amidi, LLC. Treasury for failing to report an investment by its Chinese subsidiary into embodied AI and robotics company Shanghai Qiongche Intelligent Technology (AKA Noematrix.)
US bans DeepSeek from civilian agency IT systems
The US Department of Homeland Security has ordered the removal of DeepSeek products from federal civilian agency IT systems.
The order, filed on Monday, also covers DeepSeek affiliates and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations while prohibiting affected agencies from making new purchases.
DHS warned that use of DeepSeek by government employees and contractors could expose sensitive information to China, potentially revealing details about US citizens and federal programs.
Solana’s Liu says Shanghai event postponed over registration surge
The Solana Accelerate event in Shanghai was postponed after pre-registration exceeded the event cap set by local authorities, according to Lily Liu, president of the Solana Foundation.
Event registration quadrupled overnight following publicity for the event, Liu wrote in a Friday X post, adding that organizers decided to postpone the event to “comply with local requirements.”
Earlier on Friday, X users claimed that the event was “abruptly suspended” as law enforcement officers were stationed at the venue.
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao posted he was impressed the Solana Foundation had been allowed to open a Shanghai office, noting than BNB Chain had been unable to do so.
JAPAN
Japan-Korea tourist spending becomes a test case for yen stablecoins
South Korea’s Shinhan Card has signed an agreement with Japan’s SBI VC Trade and SBI XDC Network APAC to test yen stablecoin payments for travelers and cross-border trade settlement.
Under the pact signed Tuesday, the companies will test stablecoin card payments, wallet-to-wallet payments and cross-border trade settlement. They will also assess anti-money-laundering and fraud-detection controls.
Shinhan Card is one of South Korea’s biggest credit card companies. SBI is a Japanese financial heavyweight that runs banks, brokerages, insurers and crypto exchanges.
Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal
Shareholders of Super League, a Nasdaq-listed gaming and digital media company, approved a deal that would give Japanese Bitcoin treasury firm Metaplanet a 93.7% ownership stake, paving the way for its expansion into US capital markets through a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company.
Metaplanet has also announced a planned repurchase of about $160 million of its own shares.
KOREA
South Korean finance officials met with crypto exchanges amid calls for tax delay
Finance officials reportedly met major crypto exchanges this week, days after a lawmaker introduced legislation that could push the start date of a new crypto tax back two years.
The meeting was a consultation on crypto taxation, with representatives from Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, DigitalX and Gopax, along with executives of the Digital Asset Exchange Alliance, known as DAXA.
South Korean regulators have delayed the crypto tax three times, with the latest delay pushing the start date to 2027 amid political disagreement and industry pushback.
Seoul at night. Source: Pexels, gijecho
Injective, BDACS plan Korean won stablecoin settlement for tokenized assets
Blockchain network Injective has entered into a memorandum of understanding with South Korean digital asset custodian BDACS to bring a won-backed stablecoin to its tokenized asset markets, potentially allowing institutions to settle transactions without relying on US dollar stablecoins.
Kakao plans KRW stablecoin payments ecosystem
Kakao, KakaoBank and KakaoPay have formed a new stablecoin task force to build the infrastructure required for won stablecoin issuance, custody and payments. The aim is to start with shopping and gifting.
MALAYSIA
Malaysia central bank launches DLT platform for tokenized bonds
Malaysia’s central bank has launched a distributed ledger-based platform for issuing and holding tokenized bonds, connecting digital securities records with a payment system designed to operate around the clock.
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said that its next-generation Scripless Securities Depository System (SSDS+) supports the issuance, depository and safekeeping of tokenized debt securities, including Islamic bonds known as sukuk.
THAILAND
Bitget plans Thai crypto exchange acquisition weeks after $388M hack
Crypto exchange Bitget has announced plans to acquire Thailand’s GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics, seeking to expand its Southeast Asia footprint weeks after a major hack impacting its hot and warm wallets.
The proposed transaction involves BTGT Management (Thailand), a company in which Bitget says it holds an interest, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph. The acquisition will allow Bitget to introduce its trading platform to Thai users.
Chinese suspect in $75M international crime network arrested in Bangkok
Thai police arrested a 37-year-old Chinese man wanted by authorities in China for alleged involvement in an international crime network and money laundering.
Investigators said the network handled more than 500 million yuan ($75 million) in transactions, Thai media Khaosod English reported in a post on X on Saturday.
Police alleged the suspect was involved in cryptocurrency and foreign-currency exchanges for criminal groups across more than 133 accounts. Investigators said he attempted to evade arrest by using forged documents to report his residence and changing vehicle registration plates before police found him in a luxury house in Bangkok.
VIETNAM
Da Nang crypto sandbox targets digital tourism
The fourth largest city in Vietnan, Da Nang, is using a controlled sandbox that enables businesses to employ crypto related applications in the tourism industry. Da Nang welcomed 15.9 million visitors in the first nine months of 2026.
Vietnam-EFTA agreement includes Crypto Valley links
Vietnam has signed a free-trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association countries of Switzerland, Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein. Following a meeting with the Vietnamese PM, Swiss President Guy Parmelin proposed linking Switzerland’s Crypto Valley hub with Vietnam’s innovation ecosystem to further cooperation in blockchain, AI and quantum technology.
SINGAPORE
Singapore Gulf Bank offers retail USD-stablecoin conversion
Singapore Gulf Bank (which is actually licensed by Bahrain) announced that retail customers can convert between dollars for USDT or USDC via its mobile banking app.
Singapore-backed manager launches Swiss bitcoin ETF
The Singapore backed BIT Asset Management has launched Switzerland’s first Bitcoin ETF. Formerly known as Matrixport, it’s Zurich arm has been approved by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority to launch the country’s first spot Bitcoin ETF and Europe’s only spot Bitcoin ETF.

articles.title: Circle Shareholder Targets Donald Trump’s Alleged Crypto Corruption in Lawsuit
articles.text:
Circle shareholder sues Trump, World Liberty and Steve Witkoff over crypto deals
According to a Circle shareholder, the US president’s “corruption” through USD1 left the company unable to compete with stablecoins, harming USDC.
Update (Oct. 22, 10:27 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a statement from the White House.
A shareholder for Circle Internet Financial, the company behind the USDC (USDC) stablecoin, filed a lawsuit against US President Donald Trump, his family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial, affiliate entities, and US Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff over a $2 billion deal between a foreign government entity and Binance.
In a Thursday filing in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, Circle shareholder J. Benjamin Greenberg alleged that Trump, Witkoff and World Liberty caused harm to Circle by creating a pathway for foreign governments to funnel money using the Trump family crypto company’s USD1 stablecoin. This “brazen corruption,” according to Greenberg, leaves Circle “unable to compete” in the stablecoin market with its USDC.
Central to the Circle shareholder’s allegations is an Abu Dhabi entity, MGX, tied to the United Arab Emirates royalty, which invested $2 billion into cryptocurrency exchange Binance using the USD1 stablecoin in 2025. The Wall Street Journal reported in February that another investment vehicle backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan agreed to purchase a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million.
“By accepting hundreds of millions of dollars from a foreign government, the President and his companies have diverted business from [Circle],” alleged Greenberg, adding:
“Plaintiff asks this Court to declare the President’s corrupt acts a violation of the Constitution, to enjoin the brazen corruption alleged below, to order an accounting of the billions in payments from foreign states to the President and his businesses, to require the companies holding them to disgorge the emoluments the President accepted through them, and for compensatory and punitive damages.”
Related: Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable
Greenberg reported holding 10,000 ordinary shares of Circle as part of his reasons for the lawsuit. He petitioned the court to declare that Trump violated the US Constitution’s Foreign Emoluments Clause through the crypto deals and to issue injunctions preventing the president and Witkoff from pursuing similar financial interests without Congress’ consent.
Zach Witkoff, the son of the Witkoff named in the lawsuit, is a World Liberty co-founder. Trump and his three sons are also co-founders of the crypto venture.
A Circle spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company “did not initiate, direct, authorize, or participate in the filing,” declining to comment on pending litigation. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said that Trump had “no conflicts of interest“ with his crypto investments, calling the lawsuit “frivolous.“ A spokesperson for World Liberty did not respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit.
Democrats use ’corruption’ messaging as midterm elections approach
The US president and his family are tied to several crypto ventures that Trump reported netted him $1.4 billion in 2025, while also costing investors about $4.7 billion, according to reporting by the nonprofit consumer advocacy organization Public Citizen. The crypto ventures are just a few of many controversial deals Trump faces scrutiny over, including accepting a jet from the government of Qatar.
With less than two weeks until the 2026 midterms and early voting having already started in some US states, Democrats running for reelection are using Trump’s crypto deals as a wedge issue for voters to support candidates in their party. Last week, Senator Mark Warner released a campaign ad highlighting that the president made ”more than $600 million alone from the crypto memecoin.”

articles.title: Dune Targets Institutional Traders With Onchain Market Data
articles.text:
Dune launches real-time data feeds covering 200 onchain trading venues
The new service aims to bring onchain trading data into institutional financial systems as tokenized stock markets expand and face growing scrutiny.
Blockchain analytics platform Dune has launched real-time market data feeds covering more than 200 onchain trading venues, aiming to bring decentralized market activity into the trading systems used by traditional financial institutions.
The new service provides trade data from 12 blockchains, including Ethereum, Solana, Base and XLayer, roughly one second after execution, according to a Thursday announcement.
The feeds cover spot trading across decentralized exchanges, as well as perpetual futures trading on Hyperliquid and Lighter, with standardized data on prices, trade sizes and transaction details across markets.
According to Dune co-founder and CEO Fredrik Haga, quant funds, market makers, asset managers and bank trading desks are among the first clients using the service, although he declined to identify them, citing nondisclosure agreements. Dune said the firms use the data to assess liquidity, compare prices across venues and evaluate trading strategies before committing capital.
“Most institutions are watching onchain markets first, because they can’t price these assets properly without them anymore,” Haga said. He expects direct onchain trading to follow as liquidity improves and regulatory rules catch up, adding:
What still holds institutions back is how messy it is. The same stock trades on dozens of venues across different chains, and you need to know what’s trading where before you can touch it.
Related: Ondo lets institutions convert stocks directly into tokenized shares
Tokenized stock growth brings market challenges
The market for tokenized stocks has grown sharply over the past year, but fragmented liquidity and disputes over whether companies should have a say in how their shares are traded onchain have raised questions about the market’s development.
Recently, tensions surfaced around OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange. The venture announced plans for a tokenized stock trading platform on Oct. 4, but has since faced objections from several publicly traded companies.
So far, 16 companies, including Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs, have filed objections to having their shares traded on the proposed platform, although they did not specify their reasons.
Beyond issuer objections, market fragmentation poses another concern. In May, Tiger Research director Ryan Yoon warned that trading the same tokenized stocks across multiple blockchain platforms could create price discrepancies, increase slippage and reduce market efficiency.
According to RWA.xyz data, the distributed value of tokenized stocks has reached $3.58 billion, up from about $627 million a year earlier, a roughly 470% increase.

articles.title: Crypto Today: BTC Mining Difficulty Rises, Starknet L1 Vote, PHP Security Flaw
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Bitcoin mining competition intensified as network hashrate reached a seven-month high despite the industry’s shift toward AI. Separately, Starknet voters backed research into becoming an independent layer-1 blockchain, and the PHP Foundation acknowledged delays in fixing a critical security flaw that prompted government websites to go offline.
Bitcoin mining competition heats up despite AI exodus
Bitcoin’s network hashrate has reached a seven-month high despite major mining companies shifting their computing capacity toward AI, signaling growing competition in the space, according to BlocksBridge Consulting.
Bitcoin’s seven-day average hashrate has climbed above 1 zettahash per second for the first time since March 3, suggesting that computing power leaving the network is being replaced by other miners.
Hashrate measures the computing power securing Bitcoin’s network, while mining difficulty determines how hard it is to earn new Bitcoin.
Mining difficulty increased 5.92% on Oct. 16, with BlocksBridge projecting another 5.16% increase at the next adjustment. Combined, that would represent an 11.4% increase across two adjustments, making it harder for miners to earn rewards.
The increase comes despite publicly traded mining companies reporting a 23% decline in realized hashrate as they redirect resources toward AI. Their AI-related revenue increased 52% quarter over quarter.
BlocksBridge estimates that roughly $1.5 billion worth of mining equipment has been displaced by the transition.
Some of that hardware may be finding new buyers among smaller miners with access to cheaper electricity, allowing them to expand operations while larger competitors pursue AI.
Starknet voters back research into life beyond Ethereum
Starknet’s community has voted to support research into becoming an independent, post-quantum layer-1 blockchain.
The network’s potential departure from Ethereum gained overwhelming support. The governance vote that ran for seven days closed on Thursday. The poll drew about 3,200 votes, with 93.52% of voting power in favor of the transition.
The non-binding poll recorded the highest participation in Starknet’s governance history, according to StarkWare, which said it abstained from voting to leave the decision to the community.
The outcome allows StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation to proceed with research into an independent L1. The actual shift itself would require a separate, binding governance vote. For now, Starknet will continue operating as an Ethereum layer-2 network.
“We’re beginning work on a whitepaper even before we start the weekend, and hope to release a draft for public scrutiny in November,” StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson told Cointelegraph.
PHP Foundation admits ‘structural failure’ delayed critical security fix
The PHP Foundation has acknowledged that indecision and a shortage of resources delayed a fix for a critical security flaw first identified in 2024, calling the stalled response a “structural failure.”
Government agencies and other organizations worldwide took websites offline Wednesday as a precaution while PHP released emergency patches for two related critical vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers without logging in.
PHP is a programming language widely used to power websites and web applications, including content management systems.
In a blog post following the release of the patch, the foundation described how its developers first found signs of the vulnerability in 2024, but struggled to come up with a solution without disrupting the large ecosystem of software built using PHP.
“Combined with the lack of a known path to remote code execution and the small team of core developers with the necessary deep knowledge of the engine occupied with many responsibilities, this decision process caused work on a fix to stall and restart repeatedly over months,” said the foundation.
“We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources.”
The foundation was pointed to the vulnerability again on August 11, after security firm Calif and OpenAI independently reported the same underlying issue, with Calif demonstrating unconditional remote code execution, which made it a top security priority.

articles.title: Winklevoss-Backed PAC Backs Paxton in Texas Senate Race
articles.text:
Winklevoss PAC moves into Texas Senate race with $81K ad buy
While crypto-aligned PACs have stepped up spending in Ohio, a committee launched by the co-founders of crypto exchange Gemini made one of its first forays into the Lone Star State.
Digital Freedom Fund, the Super political action committee (PAC) launched by Gemini co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2025, announced additional expenditures for US Senate races in the 2026 midterm elections, attempting to influence voters in Texas, Iowa and Ohio.
In a Tuesday filing with the US Federal Election Commission (FEC), the Digital Freedom Fund reported its first spending on ads to support Republican candidate Ken Paxton for one of Texas’ Senate seats. According to the PAC, it had spent more than $81,000 on direct mail media to support Paxton and oppose Democratic candidate James Talarico, with early voting having already begun in the state.
The Winklevoss-backed Super PAC, which reported raising about $34 million as of Sept. 30, did not limit its spending to Texas, reporting involvement in other key midterm election races using ads. Digital Freedom Fund disclosed additional expenditures in Ohio’s Senate race between Republican Jon Husted and Democrat Sherrod Brown, bringing the PAC’s total support for Husted to about $7 million.
The expenditures into candidates that could support crypto policies and laws come as event contracts on prediction market platforms Kalshi and Polymarket heavily favored Democrats retaking majority control of the House of Representatives and Senate in 2027. Whichever party holds a majority in each chamber would have a significant impact on passing legislation like the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a market structure bill that failed to pass a procedural vote in the Senate last month.
Related: PACs laud Texas primary wins, look to back more pro-crypto candidates
Paxton already benefitted from $500,000 in supportive ads ahead of the May Republican primary, in which he defeated incumbent Senator John Cornyn. The ads, funded by the Anchorage Digital- and Cantor Fitzgerald-backed Fellowship PAC, went through the Nxum Group, a marketing company co-founded by Bo Hines, a former crypto adviser to US President Donald Trump who became CEO of Tether US after leaving the White House.
According to an October Wall Street Journal report, Nxum profited from Hines’ role in government, as he helped push a stablecoin bill while keeping a stake in the company. Nxum reportedly received $6.3 million as part of a deal with stablecoin issuer Tether, the first payment of which went through while Hines was still at the White House.
Early voting began in Texas on Oct. 19, with Election Day coming up on Nov. 3. Cointelegraph reached out to the Talarico and Paxton campaign teams for comment but did not receive an immediate response.
Spending escalates in Ohio Senate race with Fairshake PAC
Fairshake, a separate PAC aligned with the interests of the crypto industry and largely funded by Ripple Labs, Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz, reported more than $13 million combined in spending on a direct mail campaign to support what it considered to be “pro-crypto” candidates this week. The PAC’s latest FEC filing showed more than $4 million to oppose Independent candidate Dan Osborn in Nebraska’s Senate race and an additional $9 million to support Husted over Brown.
While the battle for Ohio’s Senate between Brown and Husted has seen significant spending by PACs — Fairshake had invested about $56 million as of Wednesday and Digital Freedom Fund reported $7 million in total media purchases — Texas races have also spawned interest from Republican donors looking to prevent the state potentially losing Senate and gubernatorial seats to Democrats for the first time in more than 30 years.
FEC filings showed that Elon Musk, the world’s richest person and founder of SpaceX, had poured more than $150 million into the Senate Leadership Fund. The PAC, supporting Republican Senate candidates, sent the same amount Musk donated to the Texas PAC, which has supported Paxton through ads.

articles.title: Underdog Adds Stablecoin Funding as Prediction Markets Grow
articles.text:
Underdog taps zerohash to bring crypto deposits to prediction markets
The new funding option, expected to launch later this year, will allow eligible Underdog users to deposit digital assets around the clock.
Prediction market operator Underdog has partnered with crypto infrastructure provider zerohash to introduce cryptocurrency and stablecoin deposits, with the new funding option expected to launch later this year.
Eligible users will be able to fund their accounts directly through the Underdog app using supported digital assets, with the service designed to enable near-instant transfers around the clock, according to a Thursday announcement.
Underdog did not specify which cryptocurrencies or stablecoins would be supported and did not respond to Cointelegraph’s request for clarification before publication.
The new funding option will supplement existing methods, including debit and credit cards, Apple Pay and bank transfers. Users will not need to manage wallet addresses or select blockchain networks when making deposits.
Founded in 2020, Underdog has more than 11 million registered accounts, according to IG Group, which agreed in July to acquire the company in a deal worth up to $1.3 billion. The transaction is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027.
According to DeFiRate data, the company recorded $1.4 billion in trading volume over the 30 days ending Oct. 21, a 133% increase from the previous period, though it remained well behind Kalshi’s $81.5 billion and the combined $17.2 billion recorded by Polymarket’s US and international platforms.
Magazine: Agents can trade 24/7 — but Yat Siu warns you could lose access at any time

articles.title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Rises as Hashrate Recovers
articles.text:
Bitcoin hashrate hits seven-month high as AI shift fails to ease mining competition
According to BlocksBridge, Bitcoin’s mining difficulty is rising despite the industry’s AI transition, with smaller operators potentially absorbing equipment abandoned by larger competitors.
Bitcoin’s network hashrate has climbed to a seven-month high despite major publicly traded miners shifting capacity toward artificial intelligence, suggesting other operators are replacing lost computing power and intensifying competition among remaining network miners.
According to BlocksBridge Consulting’s latest Miner Weekly newsletter, Bitcoin’s seven-day average hashrate has recovered above 1 zettahash per second (ZH/s), equivalent to 1,000 exahashes per second (EH/s), its highest level since March 3.
Hashrate measures the computing power securing the Bitcoin network. The recovery suggests that miners still operating on the network are seeing little relief from competition, despite the industry’s ongoing transition to AI workloads.
Bitcoin’s mining difficulty increased 5.92% on Oct. 16, with BlocksBridge projecting another 5.16% increase at the next adjustment. If the estimate holds, difficulty will have risen roughly 11.4% across two consecutive adjustments.
“That’s hardly the breathing room remaining miners might have expected from the AI migration,” BlocksBridge wrote, referring to the growing competition facing operators that have continued mining Bitcoin.
The shift toward AI has already taken substantial mining capacity offline. BlocksBridge previously reported a 23% decline in publicly traded miners’ realized hashrate, alongside a 52% quarterly increase in their reported AI and high-performance computing revenue. It estimated that the displaced capacity represented roughly $1.5 billion in mining hardware.
Related: Crypto Biz: AI took a back seat when Bitcoin started climbing
Smaller miners may be picking up the slack
Some of the lost capacity may be returning to the network through smaller and mid-sized miners buying equipment from larger operators. BlocksBridge pointed to Sazmining, which advertises secondhand Antminer S21 XP machines that buyers can deploy through hosting facilities in Paraguay and Texas.
For miners with access to cheaper electricity, buying used machines could be more economical than investing in new equipment. It also means hardware displaced by AI conversions could continue mining Bitcoin elsewhere.
However, it’s unclear how much of the equipment being sold actually comes from publicly traded miners, or how much has returned to the network.
The hashrate recovery comes as some industry observers view rising computing power as an “indirect bullish signal” for Bitcoin, reflecting continued institutional investment in publicly traded mining companies.
CryptoQuant founder and CEO Ki Young Ju recently made that argument on X, writing that “higher hashrate means stronger security and better fundamentals as a store of value.
Related: Bitcoin miners face widening AI financing costs as lenders scrutinize deals

articles.title: Coinbase Ireland to Pay $3.6M Fine As Part of Central Bank Settlement
articles.text:
Irish cenbank fines Coinbase arm $3.6M for oversight, safeguard failures
According to the Central Bank of Ireland, Coinbase Ireland had agreed with the facts around the enforcement action and will be subject to fines and sanctions upon approval by a high court.
The Central Bank of Ireland announced an enforcement action against Coinbase Ireland for failures to safeguard user funds and provide oversight between 2020 and 2025.
In a Thursday notice, the regulator said that the Coinbase arm had “admitted the prescribed contraventions and has agreed to the undisputed facts,” settling for $3.6 million in fines. The notice said that Coinbase Ireland had violated regulations related to oversight and safeguarding of customer funds and improperly relied on the exchange’s US company to outsource certain services.
The company’s user agreement currently states: “We use a variety of service providers (some belonging to the Coinbase Group and some not) in the context of outsourcing arrangements to help us provide the Coinbase Services in an efficient and qualitative manner.”
In Thursday’s notice, the central bank’s enforcement director, Karen O’Leary, said firms operating in Ireland “must have the appropriate culture and expertise to comply with the rules, respond to risks and to protect customer interests,” adding:
“This action against Coinbase Ireland underlines the Central Bank’s focus on ensuring that customers are at all times protected and that the integrity of the financial system is maintained.”
The sanctions against the Coinbase arm require approval from Ireland’s high court before taking effect. The crypto exchange launched its operations in Ireland in 2018, receiving an e-money license from the central bank in 2019 and securing registration as a virtual asset service provider in 2022.
Related: Kazakhstan court orders curbs on Coinbase, BingX and four others

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Drops 3% as Trump Iran Comments Add to Market AI Nerves
articles.text:
Bitcoin circles $81.5K ETF cost basis as Trump Iran comments send stocks lower
Bitcoin extended daily losses to 3% as US stocks came under pressure from President Donald Trump’s comments on Iran military action.
Bitcoin (BTC) stayed below $82,000 around Thursday’s Wall Street open as Iran war headlines returned to pressure risk assets.
Key points:
- Bitcoin preserved 3% daily losses on Thursday as US stocks fell on geopolitical tensions.
- US President Donald Trump reiterated the chance of new military action against Iran, with no negotiations ongoing.
- BTC price analysis saw $84,400 as a short-term ceiling ahead of the Oct. 28 Federal Reserve meeting on interest rates.
Stocks fall as Trump says US “not negotiating” with Iran
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD hitting $81,256 on Bitstamp, down 2.9% on the day.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Mixed reactions to Tesla earnings and capital expenditures combined with a risk-off mentality stoked by fresh comments from Trump that the US was “not negotiating” with the Iranian side.
“We are going to have something one way or the other that will happen fairly soon. Most people seem to think it’s after the election and we’ll see what happens,” he told reporters, referring to the US midterm elections on Nov. 3.
US stocks fell at the open, with the S&P 500 Index down 1.3% at the time of writing. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index was 2.3% lower.
Related: Bitcoin ‘top buyers’ halt BTC price upside with $87.7K now key: Glassnode
“Tech stocks came under pressure amid renewed AI valuation fears. The rebound in energy prices contributed to the risk-off tone,” Ian Lyngen at BMO Capital Markets, told Bloomberg. He said:
“Treasuries have emerged as a primary beneficiary as global risk sentiment has come under pressure.”
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
As bond returns improved, the US 10-year bond yield approached 5% on the day, slipping to its lowest level since Sept. 23.
US 10-year bond yield one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Expect BTC in narrow range until Fed meeting
After reaching nearly $85,000 the day prior, BTC price action continued to circle the cost basis of the US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) at around $81,500.
Analysts at Bitfinex Alpha, the research arm of crypto exchange Bitfinex, on Wednesday forecast BTC/USD trading in a narrow range between $81,300 and $84,400 until the Federal Reserve rate policymakers next meeting on Oct. 28.
“Sustained ETF demand with stable leverage metrics would support a breakout above $84,400, while macro headwinds combined with a close below $81,300 would increase the risk of a move towards the 15 October low at $79,821,” the analysts wrote.
On longer time frames, traders discounted the odds of a major price recovery by mid-January 2027, with Kalshi traders trimming the chances of BTC/USD hitting new all-time highs to just 3%.
Opinion: The UK needs a workable route to regulated DeFi access

articles.title: Fireblocks Pushes Back on Reported $2.5B Visa Deal
articles.text:
Fireblocks disputes report of $2.5B Visa acquisition talks
Fireblocks told Cointelegraph that reports of a potential $2.5 billion acquisition by Visa are “not true at present time,” while Visa declined to comment on the reported talks.
Crypto custody and infrastructure provider Fireblocks is disputing a report that payments giant Visa is in late-stage talks to acquire the company for about $2.5 billion.
“We are aware of the rumors about a possible acquisition of Fireblocks by Visa. This is news to us, and not true at present time,” a Fireblocks spokesperson told Cointelegraph on Thursday.
Axios reported Thursday, citing multiple sources, that the payment giant was in advanced discussions to acquire Fireblocks for approximately $2.5 billion.
The reported price would represent a steep discount from Fireblocks’ last publicly disclosed valuation of more than $8 billion, announced by the company following a $550 million Series E funding round in January 2022. Data provider Traxcn lists the $8 billion valuation as recently as Dec. 11, 2025.
A Visa spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company does not comment on “rumors or speculation.”

articles.title: Is the Internet Safe Again After the PHP Nightmare? What You Need to Know - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- PHP's October 21 releases remain the only fix for PHP2Shell, and they protect a server only once its owner installs them and restarts PHP.
- Cloudflare's CEO said exploit attempts climbed into the millions, while Germany's BSI and Japan's government said they had not confirmed any successful break-ins.
- The PHP Foundation said it spotted signs of one flaw in 2024 and called the delay in fixing it "a structural failure."
A day after two bugs in PHP sent governments scrambling to unplug their websites, the fix is out, attackers are hammering away, and a lot of people are asking the same thing: Can I use the internet without worrying, or should I hide under the bed until next week?
The short answer is that the internet didn't break, and for most people the risk sits with the websites they visit, not with their own phones or laptops. The longer answer has a few caveats worth knowing.
Quick recap: PHP is the software that runs behind the scenes on about 70% of websites whose server-side language is known, and the two flaws, nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a stranger take control of a vulnerable server without logging in.
Is it fixed?
So, is the exploit fixed? Yes, mostly. PHP released versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 on Wednesday, according to its release notes. "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." As of Thursday, PHP has not issued any follow-up patch.
A fix only helps once someone installs it, though. PHP doesn't update itself, so every hosting company, IT department, and solo website owner has to apply it on their own servers, and then restart the software for it to take effect.
In other words, the fix is out there, but it doesn’t mean the sites you visit are necessarily safe.
PHP 8.1 and earlier no longer get official releases, which makes older servers the weak spot, although PHP's security team posted bare-bones patches for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1 for people who compile the software themselves.
Did anyone actually get hacked?
Attackers certainly tried: Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said his network saw thousands of exploit attempts in the 10 hours before the announcement, tens of thousands in the 45 minutes after it, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions since.
Some stats on #php2shell. In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the @Cloudflare network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now.
— Matthew Prince 🌥 (@eastdakota) October 22, 2026
Amazon went further, saying its decoy servers logged an attempt on October 17, four days before the bugs went public. "It remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure," Amazon CISO CJ Moses wrote, adding that PHP2Shell is "now being broadly exploited in the wild."
Governments, however, don’t seem to have experienced any sort of successful break-in yet. Thomas Caspers, vice president of Germany's federal cybersecurity agency BSI, said the agency had seen attacks but no successful use of the flaws, adding: "It seems a little bit more complicated than expected to exploit." Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary, Minoru Kihara, also said no attacks exploiting the flaws had been confirmed.
An attempt is someone rattling the doorknob; a breach is someone getting inside, so both claims can be true at once. Millions of rattled doorknobs and zero confirmed break-ins is good news, but break-ins tend to be discovered later, not in real time.
Why wasn't this caught sooner?
It sort of was. In a blog post published Wednesday, the PHP Foundation said its security work in 2024 "found the first signs of the OOM problem behind CVE-2026-109618," meaning the out-of-memory bug at the heart of one of the two flaws.
The team came up with "several competing approaches" to fix it but "struggled to choose between these and feared the repercussions of shipping the wrong choice," according to the foundation. "Without the Foundation's funding it would have been impossible to have multiple people work on this issue full time," it added.
"We won't pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team's decision process and its lack of resources," the foundation wrote, adding that its security team, which used to need consensus, will now decide by majority. For the software running most of the web, that security work "still depends on a small group of foundation-funded developers and a little volunteer help," per the post.
Why are some websites still down?
Because patching takes time, and "offline" was the official advice for anyone who couldn't patch right away. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre told organizations to consider "taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated."
The list of sites that went dark on Wednesday got long fast. According to TechRadar, it included Wikimedia services, Orange websites and apps across dozens of countries, 32 UK government services, Dutch hospitals, and Germany's federal IT provider, ITZBund.
The UK's Office for Budget Responsibility and Edinburgh's council website were back by Thursday. Others, like the Dutch anonymous crime-reporting site Meld Misdaad Anoniem, were still offline Thursday morning, according to DutchNews.
Should I change my passwords?
Not because of this, at least not yet. No confirmed data breach has been tied to PHP2Shell so far, and changing every password today won't help if a site's server is still unpatched.
What does help is the boring stuff: unique passwords for every account, two-factor authentication turned on, and paying attention if a company emails you about a breach in the coming weeks. If one shows up, change that password, and any account where you reused it.
Website owners have more homework, because patching closes the door but doesn't tell you whether someone walked in first. Security firm Tag1 advises looking for PHP files you didn't upload, new scheduled tasks, and new accounts, and rotating database passwords and API keys on any internet-facing server that ran a vulnerable version.
What about crypto?
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao had a short piece of advice on X: "Call me paranoid, but be extra careful visiting ANY web site in the next few days."
Call me paranoid, but be extra careful visiting ANY web site in the next few days, as some web admins are not always up-to-date with security patches.
Two vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) reported for PHP, the web programming language, affecting servers…
— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 21, 2026
A hacked web server can show you a fake version of a real site, and in crypto that usually means a page that asks you to connect your wallet and approve a transaction that empties it. A blockchain network itself may be fine; the websites in front of it might not be.
For the next few days, triple-check what you're signing, bookmark the sites you use instead of clicking links, and use a hardware wallet if you have one. So far, no crypto exchange has publicly reported a breach tied to PHP2Shell.
So, is it safe?
Browsing the web today is about as safe as it was last week, which is to say not perfectly. The real exposure is on servers that haven't been patched, and security company Mallory counted roughly 884,000 internet-facing hosts running PHP versions that get no official fix.
Amazon's advice to defenders is basically that this isn’t over. "Defenders should not assume the public disclosure date is the earliest date of exploitation." Any server that ran a vulnerable version since at least October 17 should be checked, not just patched.

articles.title: ChatGPT Teaches Messi Chess—On a Board It Set Up Wrong, With an Opening That Loses in Four Moves - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Lionel Messi’s Instagram ad for ChatGPT shows an AI chess lesson on a board with each side’s king and queen swapped, and drew about 1.9 million likes in a day.
- ChatGPT’s suggested “GOAT Horns” opening (1.e4 a6 2.d4 c6) allows a forced checkmate on move four from the swapped setup, but not on a correct board.
- Redditors say it is not OpenAI’s first ad with a misplaced piece, after an earlier spot reportedly put Black’s queen on e8 instead of d8.
Lionel Messi posted an ad on Instagram on Wednesday in which ChatGPT teaches him chess. The trillion-dollar chatbot flubbed the lesson so hard, Chess-knowing commentators online are losing it.
The digital board on screen in the ad has each side’s king and queen swapped, and OpenAI's chatbot recommends Messi open it up with a move that is almost guaranteed to lose in four turns.
The post, from the second most-followed person on the platform with more than 517 million followers, collected roughly 1.9 million likes and 19,600 comments in about a day.
OpenAI says more than 1.2 billion people use ChatGPT every week, and its latest pitch to them is one of the most famous athletes alive getting a chess lesson from a tutor that cannot set up the board.
If the thing sold as your all-knowing teacher fumbles move zero, it’s fair to wonder what else it delivers with a straight face.
In the post, Messi says he asked ChatGPT “to teach me a chess opening that matched my style,” and the chatbot suggested the “GOAT Horns,” a pun on the nickname Messi has carried for years. (GOAT stands for greatest of all time, for those who don’t follow sports lingo.)
Messi, of course, is known for winning games—not losing them in record time.
An opening is just the first few moves of a game. Magnus Carlsen, the world’s top-ranked player and arguably the best player in the history of the game, has played this opening, but he is also the man who played the Bongcloud—a joke opening that drags the king out on move two—against Hikaru Nakamura in 2021, so copying what Carlsen does for fun is not exactly a beginner’s syllabus.
In real chess each queen starts on a square of her own color with the king beside her, and in the ad both armies have those two pieces trading places.
The swap is not just cosmetic, because the Goat Horns moves played from that setup hand White’s queen a clear diagonal that ends up on a check mate on move four against Black—as fast as the Scholar’s mate, the fastest way to lose in Chess.
On a correct board the same moves produce no forced mate.
Reddit noticed. “How did no one like, oh I don't know, look at this for less than 5 seconds before sending it to the whole world?” pseudonymous user Cannonheim asked.
Another wrote: “Two options, either they are idiots or they are too clever, which is exactly why people are talking about it,” another one mused. A third user argued that maybe this whole thing was the fault of some random intern.
Messi asked ChatGPT to teach him a chess opening that matched his style. It suggested Goat Horns 🤘 pic.twitter.com/7w25w8LEZP
— ChatGPT (@ChatGPT) October 22, 2026
Users on r/chess said an earlier OpenAI ad had already made the same mistake, putting Black’s queen on e8 instead of d8, and one commenter wrote: “Nearly a trillion dollar evaluation and they can’t put the queen on the right square lol.”
The ad landed exactly two weeks after OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 with Intelligent UI, a feature that lets ChatGPT answer with interactive charts, buttons, and forms instead of plain text. Messi’s marketing deal with OpenAI started in June, when he posted an image made with ChatGPT Images ahead of the World Cup.
ChatGPT isn’t exactly Stockfish. Back in 2025, ChatGPT lost the final of a chatbot chess tournament, hosted by International Master Levy Rozman, after making illegal moves such as promoting pawns that did not exist but spawned out of thin air.
Thankfully, OpenAI fixed it in post and changed the pieces in a separate ad for X. The pieces are OK, the opening is still horrible to play, especially for a beginner like Messi.
The original video is still live on Messi’s Instagram.

articles.title: CryptoQuant CEO Calls Rising Bitcoin Hashrate ‘Indirect Bullish Signal’ from Institutions
articles.text:
CryptoQuant CEO calls rising Bitcoin hashrate ‘indirect bullish signal’ from institutions
Public miners backed by major TradFi players are coming back online, boosting Bitcoin’s hashrate, a positive sign for BTC’s fundamentals, according to CryptoQuant’s Ki Young Ju.
Bitcoin’s rising hashrate represents an “indirect bullish signal” from institutional investors that are backing several public Bitcoin miners, according to analytics platform CryptoQuant’s founder and CEO, Ki Young Ju.
“Higher hashrate means stronger security and better fundamentals as a store of value,” wrote Ju in a Thursday X post, adding that he sees this as a bullish signal since public miners are largely backed by traditional finance (TradFi) institutions.
Hashrate is a measure of the computational power of a blockchain network, indicating how many hash calculations are performed per second.
Bitcoin’s (BTC) hashrate has recovered by about 45% from the summer’s lows, from about 726 exahashes per second (EH/s) in July to roughly 1,050 EH/s on Wednesday, according to CryptoQuant data.
The recovery is seen by Ju as an institutional endorsement of Bitcoin’s security and long-term value as well as generally seen as a sign of confidence from BTC miners.
Still, global hashrate remained below its peak of 1,305 EH/s clocked in October 2025, when Bitcoin’s price was trading above $111,000. It was last trading at roughly $81,843 as Thursday’s US equities markets opened.
Bitcoin hashrate, Bitcoin’s price, five-year chart. Source: CryptoQuant.com
NIP Group expands Bitcoin mining capacity
Public Bitcoin miners, such as Nasdaq-listed NIP Group (NIPG), continue expanding their mining capacity, further adding to the increasing Bitcoin hashrate.
NIP Group revealed a third tranche on-rack asset purchase agreement to acquire about 4.47 EH/s of already-deployed Bitcoin mining hardware, according to a Tuesday announcement.
Once the deal closes, the machines are expected to immediately boost the miner’s Bitcoin production, with total hashrate across all three tranches expected to reach 13.85 EH/s
Related: FINMA approves Switzerland’s first Bitcoin ETF for retail investors
NIP Group currently ranks as the 16th-largest public Bitcoin miner, with 3.11 EH/s in operating hashrate. Bitdeer ranks first with 79.9 EH/s, according to Ziven data.
Top public Bitcoin miners by operating hashrate. Source: Ziven.io
NIP Group’s stock price fell 6.8% on Wednesday to close at $6.10, extending its 86% decline over the past year, according to Yahoo Finance.
Other large Bitcoin miners also saw their stock prices fall, as the US stock market suffered its sharpest selloff since July on Wednesday. TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Cipher Mining and IREN each lost about 12% from their share price, as higher-than-expected inflation figures pressured Bitcoin miners and AI infrastructure companies.

articles.title: Thailand SEC Sees No Crypto ETF Filings Despite Interest
articles.text:
Thailand SEC says several companies eye crypto ETFs, none has applied
Thailand’s SEC says several asset managers have sought consultations on spot crypto ETFs, but it cannot confirm whether the first funds will launch in 2026.
Thailand’s new spot cryptocurrency exchange-traded fund (ETF) framework is attracting interest from asset managers, but the regulator has yet to receive its first application.
Several asset management companies have approached Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for consultations about launching crypto ETFs, the regulator told Cointelegraph in a statement Thursday.
“However, no asset management company has yet submitted an application for approval to establish a crypto ETF,” the SEC said, without identifying the companies involved.
The SEC also said it was too early to determine whether the first products would receive approval before the end of 2026, noting that the timing would depend on applicants’ readiness, regulatory reviews and investor protection requirements.
Thailand’s new crypto ETF rules took effect Friday, allowing asset managers to establish locally listed spot Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) ETFs.
Several companies are already offering Thai investors BTC exposure through funds linked to overseas ETFs. ONE Asset Management became the first Thai asset manager to receive approval for a Bitcoin ETF-linked fund in 2024, while MFC Asset Management later introduced a fund investing through BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).
Related: Bitget plans Thai crypto exchange acquisition weeks after $388M hack

articles.title: a16z Drops Crypto From Its Name, Widens Bets to AI and Frontier Tech - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Andreessen Horowitz is renaming a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier, widening the fund's scope to AI and other long-horizon technologies while keeping crypto investing and regulatory advocacy.
- Chris Dixon argues blockchains have receded into the background of products from Wall Street and fintech firms, so companies should be defined by what they do, not the technology they use.
- Dixon will lead the fund with Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet.
Andreessen Horowitz, the venture capital firm better known as a16z, is renaming its crypto fund “a16z Frontier” and widening its mandate to AI and other emerging technologies, according to an email shared with its newsletter subscribers on Thursday.
a16z is among the biggest backers of the crypto industry, and when a firm that size drops “crypto” from its name, it shows where it may expect the next wave of cash to go. Chris Dixon, a general partner who runs the crypto team, says the firm’s bets include Coinbase, the blockchain network Solana, and Uniswap, a platform where people swap tokens without a middleman.
a16z calls the move “an expansion” and says crypto stays: “we will continue to invest in crypto and related ventures and advocate for sensible crypto regulation,” the firm wrote.
The argument is that blockchains—shared digital ledgers that record who owns what without a bank in the middle—have faded into the background of products people already use.
“Wall Street and fintech companies now regularly launch products built on blockchains. Does that make them crypto companies? The label matters less now,” Dixon wrote, adding that it makes more sense to define companies “by what they do rather than by the technologies they use.”
In January, a16z said it had raised more than $15 billion across its funds, and co-founder Ben Horowitz wrote in a firm post that the mission “starts with winning the key architectures of the future—AI and crypto.”
Dixon expects more “native use cases,” which he defines as “brand-new activities you couldn’t do before,” since AI so far has mostly made existing work like coding “faster, better, and cheaper.” Early versions, he says, “will look strange and unserious, like toys and hobbies,” before some grow into mainstream products.
The new label covers startups “building new technologies and creating markets that may take years to develop,” a bet Dixon says goes back more than a decade.
“When I joined a16z in 2013, I made these kinds of long-horizon investments a focus,” Dixon wrote. “The growth of smartphones made cameras, sensors, and chips better and cheaper, enabling new devices like drones, AR/VR headsets, and wearables. That theme led to investments in Oculus and drone startups like Skydio and Zipline.”
The next wave, he says, includes “autonomous machines that can perceive, reason, and act in the physical world” as well as advances in biology and medicine.
He also envisions a post-AGI society referring to artificial general intelligence, a still-theoretical AI that can match or beat humans at nearly all thinking tasks.
Crypto stays in the picture because Dixon sees it giving AI agents, meaning programs that act on their own, a way to pay each other. “Crypto can give new networks native economic capabilities, enable machine-to-machine transactions, and create new ways to bootstrap them,” he wrote.
Dixon made a similar argument in 2022, when crypto’s total market value had fallen about two-thirds from its 2021 peak. “What I look at is not prices,” he said then, pointing to developer and entrepreneur activity as the core metric.
Dixon will lead the new fund alongside a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz and general partners Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet. His post gives no size for the renamed fund, so the latest figure on record is the $2.2 billion announced in May.

articles.title: SoFi Launches Bank-Issued Tokenized Deposit Offering 4.40% APY
articles.text:
SoFi unveils bank-issued tokenized deposit for yield-bearing crypto funds
SoFi Bank launched SoFi Earn, a tokenized deposit paying 4.40% APY with FDIC coverage, allowing users to convert funds to stablecoins 24/7.
SoFi Technologies launched SoFi Earn (SOFIE) on Thursday, offering a variable 4.4% annual percentage yield on tokenized bank deposits.
SOFIE has no minimum balance requirement, according to the company’s announcement. Each SOFIE represents $1 deposited at SoFi Bank. Customers can convert it one-for-one into SoFiUSD, the bank’s dollar-pegged stablecoin, to buy crypto in its app or send funds to supported external wallets.
SOFIE deposits qualify for Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation coverage up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category. SoFiUSD carries no FDIC insurance.
On Wednesday, the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued a final rule covering payment stablecoin issuance and some custody activities, with the GENIUS Act framework taking effect in mid-January.
Cointelegraph reported in May that SoFi planned to introduce interest-bearing tokenized deposits when it made SoFiUSD available through its consumer banking app. At the time, the company said the feature would follow in the coming weeks.
The bank said SOFIE is rolling out to SoFi Crypto members through November. Members access the separate SOFIE deposit account through their SoFi Crypto account.

articles.title: Meta Creates Non-Voting Stock to Fund AI Buildout, Keeping Zuckerberg in Control - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Meta's board approved non-voting Class C stock on Oct. 19, and Class A and Class B holders will receive one Class C share per share held starting Jan. 19, 2027, in what works as a two-for-one split.
- Mark Zuckerberg holds about 60.6% of the vote on a 13.4% economic interest, and the Class C structure lets Meta sell equity without diluting that vote.
- Meta's filing says management forecasts showed a need to raise "hundreds of billions of dollars," while CFO Susan Li told analysts the company has nothing to announce on equity financing.
Meta's board has approved a new class of non-voting stock, and every holder of Class A and Class B shares will receive one new share for each share they own. The company disclosed the plan on Wednesday with its third-quarter results, and the Class C shares come into existence on Jan. 19, 2027.
The one-for-one dividend works as a two-for-one stock split, and Meta says it will not change anyone's voting power. Because Class C shares generally carry no vote, Meta can sell them for cash, or use them as pay and acquisition currency, without shrinking Mark Zuckerberg's control.
Zuckerberg held about 60.6% of the voting power on Oct. 1 against a 13.4% economic interest, according to the information statement Meta filed with the SEC. The gap comes from the dual-class setup, where Class A shares carry one vote each and Class B shares carry 10, and he beneficially owns about 341 million Class B shares.
According to the SEC filing, advisers at Moelis told the board's special committee that Meta could raise about $700 billion in equity over several years before Zuckerberg's voting power fell below 50%, according to the filing. Management also told those advisers that its long-term forecasts showed a need to raise "hundreds of billions of dollars" over several years, starting as early as fall 2026.
CFO Susan Li framed the filing's "hundreds of billions" language differently on a follow-up call with analysts, calling it "a theoretical maximum" computed to determine what level of equity financing would trigger a loss of founder control. It is "not actually a description of our present equity financing needs or plans," she said, and Meta does not have "anything to announce on that front." The structure is approved, while the size and timing of any equity sale are not disclosed.
Under a Founder Alignment Agreement signed Oct. 20, only 20% of the Class C shares Zuckerberg receives can be sold freely. Selling any of the other 80% generally requires him to sell or convert a matching Class A or Class B share within two business days, which trims his voting power.
The agreement also commits Zuckerberg to remain a California resident, or live wherever Meta is headquartered, for eight years. The filing says California's Proposition 40, a wealth tax on the Nov. 3 ballot, could make him liable for a multi-billion dollar payment, and that Zuckerberg stated selling Class B shares to cover it could cut his voting interest to about 53%.
The board has also agreed to pay another one-for-one Class C dividend each time the 30-day volume-weighted average price of Class C reaches a successive doubling of the $580.60 Class A price from Sept. 10, adjusted for splits, as long as shareholder returns compound at 10% or more a year.
Class C shares are identical to Class A and Class B except for voting rights, but the filing warns they will likely trade at some discount to Class A, and Meta may need to issue more of them for any equity sale. Class C also will not count as "voting stock" under Section 368(a) of the tax code, so sellers who want to defer taxes on a deal may push for a different structure.
Meta's board had not set the record or payment dates for the dividend as of its filing, and the payment must come within five business days after the charter takes effect on Jan. 19, 2027.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETF Flows Follow Bitcoin Prices, Don’t Predict Them: DWF Labs
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETF buyers are trend followers, not setters, DWF Labs says
DWF Labs research finds that Bitcoin ETF flows follow past BTC price movements rather than predict future returns, with investors buying rallies and selling dips.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) daily flows aren’t reliable guides to BTC’s next move as investors tend to chase rallies and sell into slumps, according to DWF Labs.
In a research report published Thursday, DWF found that investors pulled money from the funds during seven of the eight times Bitcoin’s price dropped at least 15%. All nine rallies of that size drew net inflows. The analysis reviewed 694 trading days dating back to January 2024, when Bitcoin ETFs first launched in the US.
“ETF flows confirm moves; they don’t predict them,” DWF said in its report. “The evidence points mostly to investors reacting to price, not driving it.”
Investors tended to put money into Bitcoin ETFs after prices rose and pull it out after prices fell. Those flows offered almost no clue to whether Bitcoin would rise or fall over the next five days.
Each day’s ETF flows had a moderate relationship with Bitcoin’s price changes over the five trading sessions before that day, with a correlation of 0.54. On a scale where zero means no relationship, the correlation for the following five days was 0.03.
ETF outflows don’t show who sold
The heaviest withdrawals came during the two most recent sell-offs. Investors withdrew a net $6.9 billion between October 2025 and February 2026, followed by $8.2 billion during the May–June decline.
The figures do not show whether institutions or retail investors drove the selling. DWF did not separate the two groups in its analysis.
“We don’t have a clear split on the exact buyers/sellers of the ETFs,” a DWF Labs spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
Related: Institutions held crypto through 50% drawdown, Bitwise finds
Some ETF activity also comes from investors buying fund shares while betting against Bitcoin through CME futures to earn the price gap between the two positions. DWF estimated that roughly a fifth of flows may have been hedged this way, although its data could not confirm that the same investors held both sides of the trades.
A CoinShares analysis published in June found that professional investors reduced their Bitcoin ETF exposure by 17% in the first quarter of 2026. Hedge funds and brokerages accounted for roughly 96% of the reduction, while banks increased their holdings.
Bitcoin’s sell-offs have slowed
Bitcoin has had about three sell-offs of 15% or more a year since the ETFs launched, compared with roughly four a year in 2022–2023 and eight in 2021, the report found.
The declines have also become more gradual, but the losses are still comparable. The median sell-off wiped out 21.3%, against 19.4% in 2022–2023.
“The changes aren’t solely due to the ETF,” the spokesperson said, noting that volatility and the frequency of sell-offs were already declining before the funds launched in 2024.

articles.title: Coinbase Fined Again in Ireland, This Time $3.6M Over Fund Safeguarding - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The Central Bank of Ireland fined Coinbase Ireland €3,252,618 (about $3.6 million) for breaching safeguarding and outsourcing rules between November 2020 and August 2025.
- Regulators found the firm relied too heavily on its U.S. parent for compliance, lacked local oversight expertise, and let its designated safeguarding account stay underfunded for lengthy periods; Coinbase admitted the breaches.
- It’s Ireland’s second action against Coinbase’s European business in the last year.
Coinbase’s Irish arm has been fined roughly $3.6 million by the Central Bank of Ireland for failing to properly protect customer funds, the regulator’s second enforcement action against the exchange’s European operations in less than a year.
The regulator said Thursday it penalized Coinbase Ireland €3,252,618 for breaching safeguarding and outsourcing rules under the country’s Electronic Money Regulations between November 2020 and August 2025.
The figure reflects a 30% discount off a €4,646,597 penalty for settling, which Coinbase Ireland reached with the regulator on Oct. 21. The sanction still requires confirmation by Ireland’s High Court before taking effect.
Coinbase Ireland is an e-money institution within the broader Coinbase Group, issuing the digital money customers use to buy crypto on the platform. The Central Bank found three main failures: the company leaned too heavily on its U.S.-based parent to handle safeguarding processes required under Irish and EU rules, lacked enough local expertise to oversee the protection of customer funds, and allowed its designated safeguarding account to be underfunded for lengthy periods. It also faulted the firm’s internal controls and its failure to flag material safeguarding changes to the regulator.
Coinbase Ireland admitted the breaches. Karen O’Leary, the Central Bank’s director of enforcement, said payment and e-money firms have a “fundamental obligation to fully safeguard customers’ funds” and that the regulator has “no tolerance for weaknesses in safeguarding arrangements.”
O’Leary added that failing to honor assurances made during authorization, or to report material changes, was “completely unacceptable.”
The penalty is the second Irish hit to Coinbase’s European business this year. The Central Bank fined a separate Coinbase entity, Coinbase Europe, €21.5 million in May over anti-money-laundering failures.
Coinbase has leaned on Ireland as its EU hub, securing an e-money license there ahead of Brexit and later obtaining a MiCA license to passport its services across the bloc.
The action lands even as Coinbase expands its European footprint, having recently rolled out crypto futures for traders in the region. It also underscores how the exchange’s reliance on a single jurisdiction for EU access carries regulatory risk, with Irish authorities signaling they intend to hold firms to the commitments they made to win market entry.
